title: Officers' versions of events differ
article: An Amherstburg police officer denied Tuesday punching a wounded Robert Scott Carpenter repeatedly in the head, contradicting testimony from a fellow officer that he struck him at least five times.
Const. Viktor Burany told a coroner's inquest that he slapped Carpenter twice in the head with an "open hand" in an effort to subdue him.
The testimony is consistent with statements Burany provided investigators in the days following the Oct. 30 shooting death of Carpenter, 36.
But it contradicts the testimony of Const. Rory Bennett, an officer who arrived at Carpenter's McCurdy Drive home about the same time as Burany.
Bennett testified Burany used his fist to hit Carpenter in the head at least five times. Bennett said he didn't feel the force was excessive.
Coroner's counsel Robert Ash suggested to Burany he punched Carpenter several times but Burany said Ash was "mistaken."

Burany said he never saw anyone kick Carpenter or put him in a headlock. He testified he didn't know how Carpenter suffered a series of other injuries, including neck contusions, that were discovered during an autopsy.
Burany emphatically denied allegations made by Carpenter's common- law wife, Lisa Stewart, that he planted a knife.
He declined comment when asked what he thought of the allegations.
Burany testified he saw the knife on the carpet, but never saw any blood on it because he didn't study it closely.
Bennett and Burany, who were initially dispatched to the wrong address, said they heard Const. Shawn McCurdy make a frantic call for "backup" as they raced to the scene.
They testified the front storm door was closed when they arrived and they saw no one on the front porch.
Burany, who beat Bennett into the house, said he heard someone say, "Put down the knife" as he neared the house but never heard a gunshot.
Bennett testified he heard a "loud bang" when he arrived and heard someone say, "Drop the knife" as Burany jumped on a prone Carpenter.
